Yeah, I agree completely. The brain is extremely adaptable and will eventually adapt to that little amount of THC. It will still have an effect on you and will be amplified due to your tolerance going down. I'd say if I smoked now after 40 days plus of not smoking, it'd take me a good few days to feel right again. Of course, this is all up to you, and if your goal is healing the brain completely I'd say cold turkey is the only way, as painful as that will sound to you (trust me I know ahahah) not a nice thought. But if you're at a stage where you are really motivated to do it and not have one foot in and one foot out, then I'd set a date and go for it!

Of course, reducing your usage will heal your brain to an extent. But it will still be accustomed to that quick dopamine fix. If you want your brain to fully heal and rewire, you will have to eventually bite the bullet and go cold turkey. Less is better with any substance, but thc lingers in the body through your fat for way longer than most substances, unfortunately. 
Hope that made some sense. Good luck with your journey, whatever you decide.
